- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- If sentiment is strongly bearish (≤0.2) or shows sharp reversal, model often underestimates downside; add 3–5% buffer to downside risk.
- Model frequently overshoots after recent spikes (especially >78.0) — cap forecast at +10% above prior peak unless sentiment confirms continuation.
- When sentiment shows strong mean-reversion (e.g., 0.3–0.6 over 3+ days), model tends to hold high forecasts — reduce 3–5% from forecasted peak.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.3–0.7), model often fails to capture short-term volatility — adjust for 1–2% lag in price reaction to sentiment shifts.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, model overestimates mean price when sentiment is bullish — apply 3–5% downward correction to avoid overconfidence bias.
- If sentiment shows sudden spike (e.g., 1.0) followed by drop, model often fails to adjust — reduce forecast 5–10% after spike, then allow gradual recovery.
